title: Row-DTO Vocabulary Pollution
pattern: Allowing database-specific naming conventions (such as snake_case column suffixes or prefix prefixes) to dictate the vocabulary of core domain layers.
why_bad: It pollutes the Ubiquitous Language. It forces domain experts and developers to talk in terms of database constraints (column names) rather than actual business concepts.
detection: Match struct fields or types inside domain packages containing database prefixes (`tbl_`, `row_`, `col_`) or matching specific SQL column styles.
counterexample: Low-level ORM mapper modules where mappings are defined.
fix:
Transform naming conventions at the database boundary to ensure domain models are expressed in clean Ubiquitous Language.
```rust
struct User {
    first_name: String,
    group_id: GroupId,
}
```
source: *Implementing Domain-Driven Design* by Vaughn Vernon (Chapter 6, p. 209); *Domain-Driven Design* by Eric Evans (Ubiquitous Language, p. 25).
